A tentative step in the right direction, perhaps. Something entirely new. "I went down to Pedra Purpura with Benito, everyone was there, and it was actually good. We managed to lay some ghosts to rest. It mattered, really," she confessed, offering a soft, fragile smile as she caught the profound relief washing over her aunt's face. "She said sorry, and I did too... I think we both desperately needed that closure, you know? To look the past in the eye and clear the air so there's no lingering bitterness left."

"That's wonderful, nena. Truly," Lilia said softly, wrapping both hands warmly around Agatha's fingers. "I'm so relieved to hear that. Ever since you got back, I've been telling you how vital it was to clear the air and drop that heavy luggage in the past. You both carry so much, but times have changed, and at the end of the day, we're family. Seeing you two speak to each other is healing, I really believe it's good for both of you."

"I needed it, needed to purge that poison out of my system. Talking to Wanda today made me realize that if I don't finally empty my chest, I'm never going to unglue myself from the spot. So clearing the air with Rio was massive. I've been dragging that dead weight around for years, and I finally feel lighter. At least a little."

"You're walking the right way now, nena," her aunt whispered, leaning in to press a gentle kiss to her forehead. "I'm so proud of you."

"I suppose I'm a tiny bit proud of myself, too," Agatha admitted, grimacing self-consciously in a way that had Lilia laughing outright.

"Well, you damn well should be! Now keep that momentum going: one single step at a time, my love," Lilia said, shooting her a conspiratorial wink. "And speaking of fresh starts, that invitation of Rio's sounds like a brilliant idea. You really ought to take her up on it. I bet Nicky would adore it, it'll give him a chance to socialize with other kids, and honestly, it'll buy you some breathing room to handle your own affairs."

"I'm thinking about it..." Agatha muttered, propping her chin in her hand as she stared into space. Lilia simply offered an encouraging nod, giving her shoulder one last affectionate pat before pushing herself up to head back toward the kitchen.

***

Four Years Ago

The busier she tried to keep her days, the more Agatha found herself yearning to return to work. To everyone else, her routine looked like a dream: she had everything she could possibly want, alongside the luxury of watching every single milestone of her son's early life without a single worry. Yet the bitter truth was that idleness had never suited her. She missed her own rhythm, her own purpose — Agatha genuinely missed working.

Building a career had been her life's compass from the very beginning. She hadn't chased independence just for the financial security — having grown up wealthy, money was never the hurdle — but rather for the sake of autonomy. She dreamed of earning success purely on her own merit, carving out a legitimate space for herself and winning recognition through sheer competence. That dream had cost her years of relentless grinding in law school, working twice as hard to stand out, nurturing the right alliances, and calculating every strategic move required to carve out a heavy-hitting reputation.

Following her wedding, Agatha had felt certain she was finally hitting her stride. Thanks to Tessa, she landed an enviable position right out of the gate — a massive leap ahead of anything a fresh graduate could ever manage alone. She had always imagined she would thrive under the high-stakes pressure of trial law and courtroom combat, but the reality of litigation turned out to be hollow.

She didn't truly find her rhythm until she transitioned into the conflict resolution division, which Tessa spearheaded. Working side by side with her wife on the exact same team, Agatha discovered a genuine passion for untangling messy contracts, drafting delicate settlements, and defusing disputes, vastly preferring it to the aggressive posturing and endless friction of criminal law. Eventually, she and Tessa shared the title of co-lead, steering the department together, and slowly but surely, Agatha began to shine on her own terms.

What should have been a dream scenario, however, steadily warped into an exhausting ordeal. Tessa's volatile temperament made professional collaboration a daily minefield, though Agatha constantly brushed it aside to focus on the silver lining: her growing career. She convinced herself the endless friction was just growing pains. Because Tessa craved the spotlight and demanded ample breathing room, Agatha willingly dimmed her own light, stepping back to let her wife take center stage. Deep down, it stung, but she swallowed the resentment, truly believing it was the necessary sacrifice to keep the peace at home. No matter how much Tessa sabotaged the harmony of their workday, Agatha would simply exhale, lower her head, and repeat the mantra that, despite everything, they still made a good team.

Even when she found herself constantly walking on eggshells both at the office and under her own roof, Agatha managed to convince herself she was content. Every relationship hit rough patches, she reasoned, and she truly believed Tessa was trying to do better. There were days that tested her to her core, but they were a partnership; she just needed to practice patience.

Everything shifted the moment Tessa brought up the topic of children. It felt entirely foreign to Agatha; they had always been free-spirits, bound to nothing, craving travel, adventure, and an unburdened life. Motherhood had never crossed her radar — she was fiercely in love with her independence and terrified of the crushing gravity of parental responsibility. Yet it quickly became clear how deeply it mattered to Tessa, whose frustration grew with every moment Agatha hesitated. Tessa argued it was time to settle down, insisting their love had more than enough room to spare for a family. In the end, Agatha folded. After all, they were married; building a family was simply the next logical box to check. Besides, the mere thought of that future seemed to work wonders on Tessa, making her softer, sweeter, and infinitely more present.

The path to conception, however, turned into an agonizing gauntlet that dragged Agatha straight down to rock bottom. As desperately as she wanted to walk away from the endless fertility treatments, Tessa's unyielding pressure made retreat impossible. With every failed cycle, a suffocating wave of guilt swallowed her whole — as if her deep-seated hesitation was physically manifesting inside her body, flatly rejecting the pregnancy. Yet, every time the test came back negative, Tessa only pushed harder to keep going.

When the pregnancy finally took, the journey proved just as punishing as the struggle to conceive. Agatha battled a weak cervix, a premature placental abruption, and severe preeclampsia, forcing her onto strict bed rest and away from the office mere months into the term. As her physical body suffered, her mental state unraveled right beside it, plagued by the terrifying fear that she was incapable of keeping safe the little life growing inside her heart. All she wanted was for her baby to be okay. In that dark stretch, Tessa stepped up as a devoted partner, shifting to remote work, smothering her in attentive care, and insisting Agatha step back entirely to focus on surviving. Those grueling months forged a deep closeness between them, and for the first time in ages, Agatha felt a familiar, weightless ease settle over their marriage, reminiscent of the way things used to be.

Nicky's arrival swept in a tidal wave of relief and pure joy. The delivery was smooth, the baby healthy, and both mothers were utterly intoxicated by this new chapter, drowning in adoration for the tiny human they had crafted together. Every ounce of agony had been worth it; looking down at him, Agatha knew there was no love on earth that could ever touch this.

Weeks after Nicholas was born, Tessa headed back to the office. Agatha fully intended to follow suit once her maternity leave expired, mapping out a meticulous system of nannies, daycares, and schedules to ensure their son wanted for nothing while they rebuilt their professional stride. But reality ruthlessly tore those plans to shreds. Nicky was an intensely sensitive, high-maintenance infant, prone to relentless crying spells and refusing comfort from anyone except Agatha. They cycled through a string of nannies, but none possessed the endless patience he required. They even chased down medical theories — wondering if chronic ear infections or hidden pain explained his hypersensitivity — only to find a completely healthy child. When her leave officially expired, Agatha stayed home. They scrambled for alternative compromises, but at the end of the day, only Agatha possessed the magic combination of infinite patience and soothing affection that could reach him.

Agatha tried to convince herself it was merely a phase, a matter of time before things clicked. Yet, as evening rolled in, she would frequently catch herself falling into the same old trap: staring blankly at her computer screen, skimming old case files, and aching for her career. She missed feeling useful; she missed being a distinct individual, not just a mother. Beneath it all, she just wanted to belong to herself again.

"You guys really threw a hurricane in here today."

Tessa's breezy, good-natured voice snapped Agatha out of her trance, pulling a faint smile to her lips as she watched her wife scoop up the chaotic mountain of toys scattered across the living room and toss them into a large storage bin.

"He was completely wiped out, didn't even take two minutes for him to crash."

"Well, you know how he gets whenever my godfather's in town," Agatha replied, her gaze softening as she watched Tessa. She looked so relaxed right then, genuinely trying to be present and pull her weight even after grinding through a full day at the office. They had weathered plenty of brutal fights born from Tessa's chronic absence. Agatha hated revisiting those memories, but right now, Tessa was actively proving herself, honoring her promises to do better. "Thanks for making dinner, hon."

"It was the least I could do," Tessa smiled, leaning over to press a tender kiss to her lips. "I would've loved to spend the whole day hanging out with you, but I got buried at the office."

Agatha offered an understanding nod, her eyes drifting back to her laptop screen to skim a high-stakes case file with a bittersweet tug of nostalgia.

"What on earth is that?"

Tessa's tone curdled with immediate disgust, instantly hijacking Agatha's focus. Looking up, she saw her wife holding a ratty stuffed animal by two fingers, glaring down at a cloth horse that had clearly seen much brighter decades. Agatha couldn't help the laugh that slipped out.

"It's Scratchy."

She nearly blurted out that it belonged to Benito, but caught herself, knowing all too well how Tessa reacted to the Vidal family's inescapable shadow in their lives. "It was mine when I was little, and my godfather brought it for me," she lied smoothly, recognizing the truth would only detonate an unnecessary fight.

"Babe, this biohazard needs to go straight into the trash," Tessa decreed, hiking her brows in dramatic emphasis while a playful smirk danced on her lips. Agatha parted her mouth in a mock-indignant gasp. "Look at this thing, Agatha!"

"Tessa!"

She scolded playfully, her voice dripping with mock offense. "It's a family heirloom!"

"It's a rag horse, Agatha. We can easily hire someone to stitch a brand-new, sterile replica that doesn't look like it survived a plague."

Tessa fired back with a laugh, though her eyes remained locked on the toy with undisguised contempt.

"It's not filthy, it just can't handle a washing machine, it has to be hand-washed, which is why the seams frayed a bit. It just needs a quick stitch job," Agatha defended herself, standing up to pluck the horse straight from her wife's grip as Tessa rolled her eyes. "It's just getting a makeover, that's all!"

"If you say so..."

Tessa chuckled, throwing her hands up in surrender before turning back to corral the remaining toys off the rug.

Agatha stood in silence for a few heartbeats, instinctively pulling the battered plush tightly against her chest.

"Speaking of makeovers... I've been thinking... about work."

Agatha's voice came out small, riddled with hesitation, her brows pinching together anxiously as she watched her wife freeze mid-motion, slowly turning around with genuine, unadulterated shock.

"Work?"

Agatha nervously bit down on her lower lip.

"Yeah."

She averted her gaze, giving an uneasy shrug beneath her wife's scrutiny. "I really miss the office. I know it's not the easiest time, but now that Nicky's turned two, I figured things might be a bit more manageable, don't you think? We could keep adjusting our schedule, and I could ease back into it gradually..."

"You want to go back to work? Wow... I have to admit, that caught me off guard."

Tessa arched her brows, closing the distance between them until she could cup Agatha's face, gently tucking a stray lock of hair behind her ear. Her voice turned butter-soft, laced with honeyed concern. "Are you entirely sure, sweetheart? My love, you're already stretched so thin just managing him here at home all day... It's far too much pressure to throw on yourself right now, don't you think? You don't have to prove a thing to anyone, least of all me. You don't need a job; I'm taking care of everything."

Agatha crossed her arms defensively, clutching the worn-out rag horse against her chest the exact same way she used to when she was a little girl. Tessa's expression radiated a suffocating mix of gentle worry and unyielding pressure, leaving Agatha feeling completely engulfed in a thick fog of self-doubt.

"I just... I wanted something of my own to hold onto."

"You already have me, my love."

Tessa cut in smoothly, her voice a velvety purr as her thumb traced a slow circle over Agatha's cheekbone. Agatha gave a small, defeated nod. "You have me and Nicky. Aren't we enough for you?"

"Of course you are. You're more than enough."

Agatha let out a hollow sigh. "But you know how fiercely my career mattered to me, and now... now I feel like I'm just a mother."

She let her head drop, completely beaten by the weight of her own confession. In a flash, Tessa hooked the tip of her index finger beneath Agatha's chin, forcing her gaze back upward.

"Just a mother? Sweetheart, our son literally needs you. We still haven't figured out a functional blueprint that works without you here full-time, and you're incredible with him," Tessa argued, her brows pinching together in gentle reproach. "I'd swap places with you in a heartbeat if I could, but you know my position is higher up now, and for the sake of our financial stability, it makes much more sense for me to stay on at the firm."

Agatha desperately wanted to roll her eyes, a hot flash of anger spiking through her veins before she ruthlessly forced it down. Tessa only held a higher rank because Agatha had been forced to abandon her post during a high-risk pregnancy — it had never been a choice.

"I'm here to provide everything you could ever possibly need, Agatha. Everything our baby needs, for as long as it takes," Tessa continued, her fingers resuming their soothing stroke across her jawline. "Though, of course, if having a title and a career somehow matters more to you than this family, who am I to stand in your way? You know I'm your biggest cheerleader."

"Of course not! Nicky matters more to me than anything else on this planet!"

Agatha snapped back, her brows crashing together in an irritated frown before she released a heavy, exhausted breath. "Both of you do. Our family is the most important thing in my life."

"I knew you'd see it my way, babe," Tessa smiled, giving an emphatic nod as if Agatha had just handed her a signed confession.

"I was just... thinking out loud. I know you're right."

Tessa offered a soft, sympathetic smile, her expression melting into warm compassion as she leaned in to press her lips firmly against Agatha's. Agatha closed her eyes, letting the kiss swallow her whole while instinctively shrinking inward as her wife's arms coiled around her in a tight, possessive embrace.

"Everything will fall into place when the time is right, my love," Tessa murmured right against her skin, and Agatha could only offer a numb nod. "I know it's a heavy load, and most days it's just the two of you holding down the fort, but I've got you, okay? You both mean the world to me, you're mine. Just trust me. I promise I'm doing everything I can for our family. You two are the absolute loves of my life."

***

Present Day

Agatha offered a faint, tender smile as she leaned against the doorway of her old childhood bedroom, which now belonged to Nicholas. Her son was perched cross-legged on the bed, a plump pillow propped in his lap to support his sketchpad. He was so utterly absorbed in dragging his yellow crayon across the page that he didn't even notice her slip into the room. Despite the intense concentration, his expression remained serene — his brow unknitted and his tongue caught lightly between his teeth. In the past, he would still be stewing in a sulk, but Agatha could clearly see the quiet strides he was making in self-regulation. It was yet another reassuring sign that she was finally making the right choice.

"Hey, baby," she murmured softly, stepping across the room to sit beside him on the mattress.

Nicholas looked up, curiosity flashing in his eyes, and Agatha smiled, gently threading her fingers through his wild curls.

"Do you have a minute? There's something I want to talk about." He nodded, fixing her with a steady, attentive gaze. "Remember when I asked how you'd feel about staying here at the farm with me?" He nodded again. "Well... how would you feel about making this our permanent home? Just you and me, for good?"

Nicky’s face split into a brilliant, wide-open smile, sending a tidal wave of immense relief crashing through Agatha's chest — until his expression abruptly crumpled into a frown.

"What about my mom?" Agatha choked back a gasp, genuinely stunned to hear him speak up with such quiet clarity as he stared at her with troubled doubt. "Are we never going to see her again?"

She let out a shaky sigh, biting the inside of her cheek nervously while her hand resumed its soothing rhythm through his curls.

"Do you miss her?" Agatha asked, her voice dropping to a fragile whisper. She watched as her son lowered his head, mulling it over for a long moment before giving a slow nod. "We can work it out so you spend a few days with her, maybe some weekends... If that's what you'd like, of course."

The words felt heavy in her chest. Tessa was his mother, a reality she could never erase. No matter how much she might wish otherwise, Agatha couldn't simply excise her from their lives, and she knew Tessa would fight tooth and nail to prevent it anyway.

"Is this what you want?" she gently pressed, searching his face with hopeful expectation.

Nicholas didn't answer right away, just held her gaze with unwavering directness, leaving Agatha to guess. Usually, she didn't struggle to read him; she often felt like Nicky communicated through his eyes, letting her know his mind even in total silence. But every now and then, in moments like this, she felt completely blind. He just stared at her, as if trying to decode her thoughts just as desperately as she was trying to decode his.

"It's just going to be you and me for right now, okay?" she said carefully, and he offered a small nod. "We're going to look at finding our own house, and you'll get to design your bedroom however you want with everything you've ever dreamed of." She gave his ribs a playful poke, coaxing a soft giggle out of him. "And I talked to Wanda…”

Nicholas raised a single eyebrow, his grin lingering. She had noticed how quickly he had warmed up to Wanda and how comfortable he felt around the boys.

"She told me you can start going to school right here, and I heard it's practically next door to the racetrack where the horses run."

The moment those words left her mouth, Nicholas's face lit up with a massive, triumphant grin, his entire body bouncing with electric excitement and dragging a joyful laugh straight out of Agatha. She might not always have a translation for his silence, but she could read the pure happiness radiating off him clear as day. She knew things with Tessa would inevitably get messy, but right now, they were safe, they were stable, and that was all that mattered.

"Want to know who else I talked to? Rio."

Simply dropping that single name was like striking a match. Nicholas's face blazed with a smile so radiant it could have lit up the entire valley, sending a rush of warmth straight to Agatha's heart. He planted both hands on her shoulders, giving her a little shake to hurry her along.

"She invited you down to the racetrack. Said she could teach you how to ride. What do you think?"

"Yes! Yes, Mom!" he blurted out, euphoric.

Agatha burst into a laugh of pure, unadulterated delight. She drank in the moment, completely melting as he launched himself against her chest, rocking them both back and forth as they laughed together.

Yes, they were going to be just fine. They were finally home.
